newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: WB sees Manila needing $9 bln/yr financing to 1998.
newsitem.headline: WB sees Manila needing $9 bln/yr financing to 1998.

text.p: The World Bank (WB) said the Philippines needs an average of $9 billion of external financing in the next two years to finance its different infrastructure projects, a study released on Thursday said.
The study said most of the financing would come from the private sector which will put in the money as part of equity investment.
The Philippines needs $8.9 billion in external funds next year, and $9.1 billion in 1998, it said.
Private capital would contribute $7.1 billion in 1997 and $7.3 billion in 1998, while official development assistance would contribute $1.8 billion in each year.
In 1996, the Philippines attracted $9.3 billion worth of external financing, up from $5.0 billion in 1995.
